messages:
deploy-bot: publish failed for repo=redwood/inference-runtime region=eu-west-1. manifest upload accepted but validation failed: DigestMismatchError manifest=sha256:AAA111 computed=sha256:BBB222. provenance check failed -> blocking release.
elaine: on it — which build id and runner?
deploy-bot: build_id=build-6912 timestamp=2026-03-18T04:12:03Z tag=runtime:2026.03.18 image_sha=sha256:AAA111
sam: I saw this pattern before — usually caused by chunked multipart push where a retry resumes an older upload session and layer order gets mixed. @kevin can you check the CI runner logs for concurrent pushes?
kevin: checking now. CI logs show two overlapping pushes: one aborted mid-chunk, the retry reused the uploadSessionId and pushed chunks in a slightly different sequence. ECR accepted layers but manifest assembly picked a different ordering -> digest mismatch.
michelle: if it's just layer-order, layers themselves might be intact. We can try to reconstruct the manifest locally from the layer blobs and repush. Can we pull the blobs by their digests? ECR allows GetBlob if we have the upload session.
elaine: immediate plan: hold the release window. Pin canary / traffic to previous stable digest runtime:2026.03.11 sha256:old111. release-manager please update release notes + rollback plan and notify stakeholders.
release-manager: acknowledged — holding the change window for 2h, updating notes and incident INC-2026-113. Will add a short blurb to the release channel.
sam: remediation proposal: avoid republishing same tag. Retag as runtime:2026.03.18-hotfix1 and repush from a single dedicated runner that does not reuse upload sessions. Steps I suggest:
```
# on builder node that has the image artifacts
docker save redwood/inference-runtime:runtime-2026.03.18 -o /tmp/runtime.tar
# load into a clean runner and re-push using skopeo to avoid docker client chunk-session bugs
sudo skopeo copy --retry 5 docker-archive:/tmp/runtime.tar docker://123456789012.dkr.ecr.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/redwood/inference-runtime:2026.03.18-hotfix1
# then cosign attest and push provenance
cosign sign-blob --key $COSIGN_KEY /tmp/runtime.tar && cosign attest --predicate predicate.json ...
```
kevin: I'll run the repush on a fresh ephemeral runner now, will ensure no concurrent pushes and monitor layer ordering. If repush succeeds I'll trigger deploy-bot to validate.
michelle: I'll open a CI PR to stop reusing uploadSessionId during retries and add an integration test that simulates chunked retry. PR will reference INC-2026-113.
elaine: good. If repush fails, we escalate to AWS support for ECR-upload-session investigation. @deploy-bot will you revalidate automatically once new tag detected?
deploy-bot: yes — will auto-validate new tags and post results to this thread. Current block tracked as INC-2026-113.
kevin: quick update: repush started (runner=runner-87). if successful I'll update canary policy to point at :2026.03.18-hotfix1 and kick canary deploy.
sam: also adding a note to the release notes: "Publish hiccup due to chunked-upload reordering; release delayed, retagged hotfix; CI fix incoming."
elaine: thanks team — keep updates short here. If we have a clean push before +2h we'll proceed, else rollback plan will remain active.
